research_question: What concurrency, snapshot, checkpoint, durability, portability, and version boundaries does SQLite WAL actually impose on a single-authority local UnifiedDB substrate?

project_sources.relevance: F2-WP-100 canonical UnifiedDB accepted only at bounded repository-evidence scope; later integration/runtime credit remains separate.
One canonical installed state lineage, local-first portability, explicit minimum runtime dependencies, restart/recovery and durable-state readback are product requirements.

Current Trigger-6 research database uses Python sqlite3 but explicitly declares itself a research/evidence index rather than canonical world truth; this is evidence of SQLite usage, not evidence of canonical UnifiedDB runtime configuration.

source_verified_findings.finding: WAL allows concurrent readers and a writer, but SQLite still permits only one writer at a time. Writes are serialized across connections.
source_verified_findings.implication: Do not equate WAL with parallel write throughput or multiple simultaneous canonical writers.

source_verified_findings.finding: A WAL reader sees a stable snapshot from the start of its read transaction; later commits remain invisible until that read transaction ends and a new one begins. Read-to-write escalation can fail with SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT when the snapshot is stale.
source_verified_findings.implication: Long-lived reasoning/model/tool work must not assume an open read transaction remains current canonical state. Materialize a bounded snapshot, close the transaction, and re-enter/revalidate before authority-sensitive writes.

source_verified_findings.finding: Long-running or continuously overlapping readers can prevent checkpoints from completing and can let the WAL grow without bound.
source_verified_findings.implication: Canonical-state readers should avoid holding DB read transactions across long cognition/tool/provider latency; checkpoint health and WAL growth require explicit observability.

source_verified_findings.finding: BEGIN IMMEDIATE can fail with SQLITE_BUSY when another write transaction is active; WAL-mode queries can also return SQLITE_BUSY in documented recovery/locking cases.
source_verified_findings.implication: Writer contention is a first-class control-plane condition requiring bounded backoff/arbitration and measurement, not an exceptional impossible state.

source_verified_findings.finding: WAL requires shared-memory coordination and therefore all database users must be on the same host; WAL is not a network-filesystem multi-host coordination mechanism.
source_verified_findings.implication: Remote/VPS organs cannot share canonical local SQLite WAL as though it were distributed state authority; they require typed transport/projection boundaries.

source_verified_findings.finding: With synchronous=FULL the WAL is synced on transaction commit; with synchronous=NORMAL SQLite explicitly allows recent transactions to roll back after power loss or hard reset. Checkpointing has separate sync/performance behavior.
source_verified_findings.implication: Canonical state/evidence must declare its durability tier; performance-oriented NORMAL must not silently inherit a stronger crash/power-loss claim.

source_verified_findings.finding: The WAL file is part of database persistent state while present; separating/copying the main database without its WAL can lose committed transactions or corrupt the copied state.
source_verified_findings.implication: Backup/migration/release acceptance must use a quiesced/checkpointed or SQLite-supported backup procedure rather than raw-copying the .db file alone while active.

source_verified_findings.finding: SQLite documents a rare WAL-reset data race capable of corruption when two or more connections in separate threads/processes perform concurrent write/checkpoint timing. The affected range is reported as 3.7.0 through 3.51.2; fixed in 3.51.3 and later, with listed backports 3.44.6 and 3.50.7.
source_verified_findings.implication: If F2 uses WAL with multiple connections, release/runtime capability evidence must bind the actual SQLite library version and reject a vulnerable version unless an explicitly verified fixed backport is present. This research does not establish which SQLite version the target F2 host currently loads.

counterhypothesis.statement: SQLite's internal locking is sufficient by itself, so F2 needs no explicit writer-arbitration, snapshot-reentry, checkpoint-health, or SQLite-version contract.
counterhypothesis.reason: SQLite serializes writers but surfaces BUSY/BUSY_SNAPSHOT, permits checkpoint starvation, exposes configurable durability, has same-host WAL constraints, and currently documents a version-specific concurrent WAL corruption race. Internal locking prevents many invalid interleavings but does not supply the product-level scheduling, freshness, durability, observability, portability, or dependency-evidence contract F2 requires.

proposed_invariants: Exactly one canonical local SQLite authority; WAL never becomes a distributed multi-host authority.
Record actual SQLite runtime version, journal_mode, synchronous setting and connection topology in host/runtime evidence before granting WAL concurrency/durability credit.
If WAL uses two or more concurrent connections, require SQLite >=3.51.3 or a specifically verified fixed backport before accepting concurrent write/checkpoint operation.
Treat one-writer serialization and SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT as explicit measured control states with bounded retry/backpressure rather than hiding them in unbounded loops.

Never keep a canonical-state read transaction open across long model/tool/network work; close after bounded snapshot extraction and re-enter/revalidate generation/state before authority-sensitive mutation.
Expose WAL size/checkpoint progress/reader-age signals so checkpoint starvation is falsifiable.
Declare canonical write durability semantics explicitly; do not claim power-loss durability from synchronous=NORMAL.
Use a safe SQLite backup/quiesce/checkpoint procedure for active WAL databases; do not copy the main database file alone.

highest_information_next_discriminator.owner: Triggerword 4 integration/test lane after E2 architecture mapping
highest_information_next_discriminator.action: At exact target runtime/package identity, record sqlite3 library version + journal_mode + synchronous + connection/process topology, then run a bounded two-writer/long-reader/checkpoint contention probe and verify BUSY handling, snapshot freshness, checkpoint progress, restart integrity and no hidden second state authority.
highest_information_next_discriminator.acceptance_boundary: This E1 source result grants zero F2 runtime, integration, durability, concurrency, or whole-system credit.

negative_evidence: No current target-host SQLite library version was observed in this research iteration.
No evidence was found that the accepted-at-repository-scope F2-WP-100 currently enables WAL or satisfies the proposed WAL runtime fences.
No runtime contention, power-loss, crash-recovery, checkpoint-starvation, or corruption test was executed in Trigger 6.
closure: E1 source extraction is saturated enough for a bounded next-stage E2 architecture mapping; no implementation was performed.
